hints.content:
A dilation by a scale factor of $\goldD{\dfrac13}$ means that all the distances in the image are $\dfrac13$ as long as they were in the pre-image. We don't have exact measurements, but that's shorter than half the lengths in the pre-image.

Also, each point in the image lies on the line connecting its corresponding point in the pre-image and the center of dilation $P$. Since $\goldD{\dfrac13}<\dfrac12$, the point in the image should lie *between* the two points, and *closer to $P$* than to the pre-image.

These two options have lengths that are shorter than half the lengths in the pre-image.



[[☃ image 1]]

 

[[☃ image 2]]

Out of these two, only the first option has the image points lying between their pre-image and $P$.
